title: Indo-Pakistani War of 1947–1948
summary: First Kashmir War fought over the princely state of Kashmir immediately after independence.
contextSummary: Following the partition of India, Pashtun tribal militias from Pakistan invaded Jammu and Kashmir.
outcomeSummary: Ceasefire orchestrated by the UN, establishing the Line of Control.
content: The First Kashmir War was the first of four Indo-Pakistan Wars fought between the two newly independent nations. Pakistan precipitated the war a few weeks after independence by launching tribal lashkar (militia) from Waziristan. The conflict saw intense fighting across the mountainous terrain of Kashmir and established the borders that largely define the region today.

title: Annexation of Goa (Operation Vijay)
summary: Military action by the Indian Armed Forces that ended Portuguese colonial rule in Goa, Daman, and Diu.
contextSummary: Portugal refused to negotiate the handover of its enclaves in India after independence.
outcomeSummary: Decisive Indian victory and integration of Goa, Daman, and Diu into India.
content: The Annexation of Goa was the process in which the Republic of India annexed Estado da Índia, the former Portuguese Indian territories of Goa, Daman and Diu, starting with the armed action carried out by the Indian Armed Forces in December 1961. It was a swift operation involving air, sea, and land strikes.

title: Sino-Indian War
summary: A brief border conflict with China along the Himalayan frontier over territorial disputes.
contextSummary: Tensions arose over the disputed Himalayan border and India's granting of asylum to the Dalai Lama.
outcomeSummary: Chinese military victory and assertion of control over Aksai Chin.
content: The Sino-Indian War was a war between China and India that occurred in 1962. A disputed Himalayan border was the main cause of the war. There had been a series of violent border skirmishes between the two countries. The war highlighted significant vulnerabilities in India's military readiness.

title: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
summary: The second major war against Pakistan, beginning after Operation Gibraltar.
contextSummary: Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar was designed to infiltrate forces into Jammu and Kashmir to precipitate an insurgency.
outcomeSummary: Inconclusive; UN-mandated ceasefire, followed by the Tashkent Declaration.
content: The Indo-Pakistani War of 1965 was a culmination of skirmishes that took place between April 1965 and September 1965 between Pakistan and India. The conflict began following Pakistan's Operation Gibraltar, which was designed to infiltrate forces into Jammu and Kashmir to precipitate an insurgency against Indian rule.

title: Indo-Pakistani War of 1971
summary: A decisive war that led to the liberation of East Pakistan and the creation of independent Bangladesh.
contextSummary: The Bangladesh Liberation War led to millions of refugees pouring into India.
outcomeSummary: Decisive Indian victory, creation of Bangladesh.
content: The 1971 war was a swift and decisive conflict. In the east, the Indian Army and Mukti Bahini outflanked Pakistani defenses, racing to Dhaka. In the west, Indian forces held off Pakistani offensives and made significant territorial gains. The war ended with the surrender of Pakistani forces in Dhaka.

title: Siachen Conflict (Operation Meghdoot)
summary: A strategic military operation to secure control over the Siachen Glacier.
contextSummary: Intelligence suggested Pakistan was planning an operation to occupy the Siachen Glacier.
outcomeSummary: Indian forces successfully gained control of the entire Siachen Glacier.
content: Operation Meghdoot was the code-name for the Indian Armed Forces' operation to capture the Siachen Glacier in the Kashmir region, precipitating the Siachen conflict. It was the first assault launched in the highest battlefield in the world. The military action resulted in Indian troops gaining control of the entire Siachen Glacier.

title: Kargil War
summary: A high-altitude armed conflict fought in the Kargil district of Kashmir against Pakistani infiltrators.
contextSummary: Pakistani forces and Kashmiri militants infiltrated into positions on the Indian side of the LOC.
outcomeSummary: India successfully recaptured all positions infiltrated by Pakistani forces.
content: The Kargil War was an armed conflict between India and Pakistan that took place between May and July 1999 in the Kargil district of Kashmir and elsewhere along the Line of Control (LoC). The conflict was characterized by high-altitude mountain warfare, which posed significant logistical and tactical challenges.
